title: List Products Response
description: Canonical product offers and continuation state. Every product carries product_id and name; other compact detail fields follow the request's fields selection. Legacy named-format identifiers are never returned. This response never contains proposals or proposal-lifecycle fields.

adcp_version.description: Release-precision AdCP version (VERSION.RELEASE, e.g. "3.0", "3.1", "3.1-beta"). On a request: the buyer's release pin — the seller validates against its supported_versions and returns VERSION_UNSUPPORTED on cross-major mismatch, or downshifts to the highest supported release within the same major. On a response: the release the seller actually served — clients SHOULD validate the response against that release's schema, not against their pin. Patches are not negotiated; surface them as build_version on capabilities for operational visibility. When omitted, falls back to adcp_major_version (deprecated) or server default. Buyers SHOULD emit both adcp_version and adcp_major_version through 3.x to remain compatible with sellers that only read the legacy field. NORMALIZATION: SDKs that read full-semver values from bundle metadata (e.g. ComplianceIndex.published_version = "3.1.0-beta.1") MUST normalize to release-precision ("3.1-beta.1") before emitting on the wire — meta-field values are NOT valid wire values.

outcome.description: Whether this response carries a product page or confirms that the selected feed has not changed.

items.title: Canonical Product
items.description: Standalone compact Product view for the AdCP 3.2 lifecycle. product_id and name are the only always-returned fields; requested detail fields are optional. Legacy named formats, coarse MediaBuy actions, and the legacy Product inheritance graph are absent.

creative_policy.title: Creative Policy
creative_policy.description: Product creative requirements, including optional review_sla.

review_sla.title: Creative Review SLA
review_sla.description: Product-scoped time to an approved or rejected decision for accepted formats. Separate from the sync_creatives action SLA, which covers ingestion. Current buy actions resolve review_sla for applicable packages; absence means no review commitment.

allOf.title: SLA Window
allOf.description: Optional commitment; absence means none, not zero. Duration predicates MUST require presence. Elapsed time includes non-working time (P1D = PT24H). Business time uses the referenced calendar's working periods and business_day_minutes for P1D. Compare clocks using deadlines for the same receipt time.

clock.description: Business time starts at seller receipt, advancing to the next working period when outside working time.

business_calendar_id.description: Immutable seller-local ID in get_adcp_capabilities.business_calendars; required only for business time.

response_max.description: ISO 8601 acknowledgement bound: synchronous response for self_serve, tolerance decision for conditional_self_serve, queue receipt for seller_managed/requires_approval. Elapsed action SLAs start at buyer issuance. Review and report SLAs start at seller receipt; reports require human acknowledgement.

completion_max.description: ISO 8601 completion bound: mutation applied, proposal finalized, or seller-managed decision resolved. Elapsed action SLAs start at buyer issuance. Review SLAs start at seller receipt and complete at an approved or rejected decision.

verifier_constraints.calendar_reference: A business_calendar_id resolves to exactly one immutable get_adcp_capabilities.business_calendars declaration whose coverage includes receipt and the computed deadline. Invalid or unresolved calendars never fall back to elapsed time.
verifier_constraints.request_snapshot: Pending requests retain the SLA and calendar resolved at receipt. Maxima are independent upper bounds; a completion maximum shorter than the response maximum does not invalidate either commitment.

provenance_required.description: Whether creatives must include provenance metadata. When true, the seller requires buyers to attach provenance declarations to creative submissions. The seller may independently verify claims via get_creative_features.

provenance_requirements.description: Structured provenance requirements for creatives. Refines `provenance_required`: when `provenance_required` is true, the fields in this object specify which provenance features the seller requires. When `provenance_required` is false or absent, this object SHOULD be absent; if present, receivers MUST ignore it. Existing seller agents that do not read this object are unaffected; the wire shape does not change for them. Sellers that publish a requirement here MUST enforce it on creative submission: a `sync_creatives` request that omits a required field is rejected with the corresponding `PROVENANCE_*` error code (see error-code.json), and a creative whose provenance claim is contradicted by an independent verification (`get_creative_features` against a governance agent the seller operates or has allowlisted via `accepted_verifiers`) is rejected with `PROVENANCE_CLAIM_CONTRADICTED`. This is the structural-rejection surface; the truth-of-claim surface lives in `get_creative_features`. Field-level requirements are seller-enforced — JSON Schema validation does not check them.

require_digital_source_type.description: When true, the seller requires creatives to include a `digital_source_type` field in their provenance, set to a valid value from the `digital-source-type` enum (not null or absent). Submissions that omit this field are rejected with `PROVENANCE_DIGITAL_SOURCE_TYPE_MISSING`. Supports EU AI Act Art. 50 and CA SB 942 compliance workflows where AI disclosure metadata must be present at the protocol level.

require_synthetic_depiction.description: When true, the seller requires creatives to include an assessed `synthetic_depiction` boolean in their resolved provenance. Both true and false satisfy the requirement; absence means unassessed and is rejected with `PROVENANCE_SYNTHETIC_DEPICTION_MISSING`. This gate requires a declaration only — it does not establish consent, legality, or independent verification.

require_disclosure_metadata.description: When true, the seller requires creatives to include a `disclosure` object in their provenance with `disclosure.required` set to a boolean value (true or false). When `disclosure.required` is true, at least one entry in `disclosure.jurisdictions` is expected. Submissions that omit `disclosure.required` are rejected with `PROVENANCE_DISCLOSURE_MISSING`.

require_embedded_provenance.description: When true, the seller requires creatives to include at least one `embedded_provenance` entry. For pipelines where sidecar metadata is stripped by intermediaries, this ensures provenance data persists through delivery. Submissions that omit `embedded_provenance` are rejected with `PROVENANCE_EMBEDDED_MISSING`.

accepted_verifiers.description: Governance agents the seller operates, has allowlisted, or otherwise trusts to verify provenance claims via `get_creative_features`. Buyers attaching a `verify_agent` pointer on `embedded_provenance[]` or `watermarks[]` MUST select an `agent_url` that appears in this list (canonicalized per /docs/reference/url-canonicalization: lowercase scheme and host, strip default port, normalize path dot-segments) - the buyer is *representing* that they used a verifier the seller will recognize, not asserting unilateral routing. Sellers MUST reject `sync_creatives` submissions whose `verify_agent.agent_url` does not match any entry here with `PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_NOT_ACCEPTED`. The seller is the verifier-of-record: it is the seller, not the buyer, that decides which agent it will call. Publishing the list lets buyers pre-flight their creative shape against `get_products` and lets multiple buyers converge on the same verifier without coordinating with each other.

agent_url.description: URL of the governance agent. MUST use the `https://` scheme. The seller calls this URL via `get_creative_features` to verify a buyer's claim; the seller has already vetted the endpoint and accepts responsibility for outbound calls to it.

feature_id.description: Optional canonical `feature_id` the seller will request against this agent (e.g., `encypher.markers_present_v2`). When present, the buyer's `verify_agent.feature_id` SHOULD either match this value or be omitted. When absent, the seller selects a feature from the agent's `governance.creative_features` catalog at evaluation time. Resolves the selector ambiguity that would otherwise let two compliant receivers reach different verdicts.

providers.description: Optional `provider` labels this agent verifies (e.g., `['Encypher', 'Digimarc']`). When present, sellers SHOULD only invoke this agent for `embedded_provenance[]` / `watermarks[]` entries whose `provider` field matches one of these labels — letting buyers pre-flight whether their attached evidence is verifiable against the seller's allowlist. When absent, the agent is treated as provider-agnostic.

publisher_properties.description: A non-empty array is the complete roster. `[]` means undisclosed, not no properties. MUST NOT be `[]` below 3.3.

allOf.title: Publisher Property Selector
allOf.description: Selects properties from a publisher's adagents.json. Used for both product definitions and agent authorization. Supports three selection patterns: all properties, specific IDs, or by tags. Each selector targets one publisher via `publisher_domain` (string) or a fan-out across many publishers that share the same selector via `publisher_domains` (array). Exactly one of `publisher_domain` or `publisher_domains` MUST be present. When `publisher_domains` is used, the selector is logically equivalent to repeating the same entry once per listed domain.

oneOf.description: Select all properties from one publisher domain, or from each publisher domain when `publisher_domains` is used. Consumers MAY satisfy the selector from the parent file's top-level `properties[]` when those properties carry a `publisher_domain` matching one of the listed domains (see Resolution paths in the spec).

publisher_domain.description: Domain where publisher's adagents.json is hosted (e.g., 'cnn.com'). XOR with `publisher_domains` — exactly one MUST be present on each `publisher_properties[]` entry; both-present and neither-present both fail validation.

publisher_domains.description: Compact form for fanning the same selector across many publishers (e.g., a managed network listing every publisher it represents). Each entry is the domain where that publisher's adagents.json is hosted. Each listed domain MUST be canonicalized to lowercase (the `pattern` already rejects uppercase). Mutually exclusive with `publisher_domain`. Each listed domain counts as explicitly scoped for the `managerdomain` fallback safety rule.

selection_type.description: Discriminator indicating all properties from each addressed publisher are included

oneOf.description: Select specific properties by ID. Single-publisher only — property IDs are publisher-scoped, so the compact `publisher_domains[]` form is intentionally NOT available for this selector. Use multiple `publisher_properties[]` entries (one per publisher) when each publisher's ID set differs.

publisher_domain.description: Domain where publisher's adagents.json is hosted (e.g., 'cnn.com').

selection_type.description: Discriminator indicating selection by specific property IDs

property_ids.description: Specific property IDs from the publisher's adagents.json

items.title: Property ID
items.description: Identifier for a publisher property. Must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores only.

oneOf.description: Select properties by tag membership. With `publisher_domains`, the same `property_tags` predicate is resolved against each listed publisher's adagents.json — the common managed-network case where every represented site tags inventory with a shared label. Consumers MAY also satisfy the predicate from the parent file's top-level `properties[]` when those properties carry a `publisher_domain` matching one of the selector's `publisher_domains[]` (see Resolution paths in the spec).

publisher_domain.description: Domain where publisher's adagents.json is hosted (e.g., 'cnn.com'). XOR with `publisher_domains` — exactly one MUST be present on each `publisher_properties[]` entry; both-present and neither-present both fail validation.

publisher_domains.description: Compact form for fanning the same tag predicate across many publishers (canonical managed-network shape). Each entry is the domain where that publisher's adagents.json is hosted. Each listed domain MUST be canonicalized to lowercase (the `pattern` already rejects uppercase). Mutually exclusive with `publisher_domain`. Each listed domain counts as explicitly scoped for the `managerdomain` fallback safety rule.

selection_type.description: Discriminator indicating selection by property tags

property_tags.description: Property tags resolved against each addressed publisher's adagents.json, OR against the parent file's top-level `properties[]` when those properties carry a `publisher_domain` matching the selector. Selector covers all properties carrying any of these tags.

items.title: Property Tag
items.description: Tag for categorizing publisher properties. Must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores only.

items.title: Canonical Format Option
items.description: Compact canonical creative-format declaration. Legacy named-format links are intentionally absent; params are validated against the canonical schema selected by format_kind without inlining every format union into product discovery. Format-option processing metadata such as macro_resolution_capabilities stays at this object's top level and is not part of canonical params.

tracker_execution_contract.title: Tracker Execution Contract
tracker_execution_contract.description: Seller- or publisher-authored production commitment for first-class manifest tracker execution. Presence requires a stable format_option_id. Creative-agent projections MUST strip this authority-bearing field.

complete.description: Whether honored is the complete set. complete:true with an empty honored array explicitly supports no buyer-supplied trackers.

items.title: Tracker Execution Selector
items.description: One exact first-class manifest tracker selector in a seller production execution contract. AdCP 3.2 supports pixel_tracker, vast_tracker, and daast_tracker only; URL-slot selectors are not part of this union.

selector_id.description: Stable identifier unique within the materialized execution contract.

method.description: AdCP 3.2 execution contracts cover image-pixel initiation only; JavaScript response evaluation is outside this contract version.

custom_event_name.description: Required only when event is custom.

firing_paths.description: Complete set of permitted initiation environments. Exactly one path is selected for each logical event occurrence.

selector_id.description: Stable identifier unique within the materialized execution contract.

firing_paths.description: Complete set of permitted initiation environments. Exactly one path is selected for each logical event occurrence.

allOf.title: VAST Tracker Constraints
allOf.description: Shared VAST TrackingEvents constraints used by tracker assets and production execution selectors. The target/event matrix is closed, progress alone carries offset, and selector version arrays may contain only versions in which the event exists.

allOf.$comment: VAST 4.0 omitted closeLinear; VAST 4.1 restored it from VAST 3.0. The 4.0 gap is intentional.

selector_id.description: Stable identifier unique within the materialized execution contract.

firing_paths.description: Complete set of permitted initiation environments. Exactly one path is selected for each logical event occurrence.

allOf.title: DAAST Tracker Constraints
allOf.description: Shared DAAST tracker vocabulary and execution-selector constraints. The legacy asset vocabulary retains AdCP's historical close extension, while the closed standards selector matrix excludes it. Progress alone carries offset in selectors.

honored.description: Exact tracker/event selectors the seller accepts and initiates once per manifest instance for each logical event occurrence. selector_id and structural selector identity are each unique within this array.

x-adcp-validation.version_sets: For one non-version selector identity, version sets must be identical or disjoint; overlapping unequal sets are invalid.
x-adcp-validation.asset_normalization: Before selector matching, omitted pixel_tracker.method becomes img, omitted VAST/DAAST target becomes linear, and offset on a non-progress asset is ignored and removed. Existing 3.x asset schemas remain structurally permissive; the selector schema supplies the closed event/target matrix for contract matching.
x-adcp-validation.format_slot_satisfiability: Every asset_type named by honored MUST have at least one matching first-class slot in the effective selected canonical format declaration. A contract cannot promise execution for an asset shape that the same format rejects structurally.
x-adcp-validation.layer_derivation: Publisher, placement, and seller effective-contract derivation is evaluated over atomic tuples of normalized non-version selector identity, one exact version (or null for pixel), execution_actor, and one firing_path. For a complete parent, every child tuple MUST exist in the parent, the child remains complete, and array compression MUST NOT create a version/path cross-product. An incomplete or omitted parent is not a ceiling: a child may add or omit affirmative tuples for its narrower scope, but remains incomplete until every applicable layer is complete. Omission from an incomplete child is undeclared, not an assertion that the tuple is unsupported.
x-adcp-validation.cardinality: Each accepted manifest tracker instance is initiated exactly once in total for each logical event occurrence; identical URLs are not deduplicated.

items.title: Macro Processing Capability
items.description: One exact processing capability for one governed dialect semantic, operation, actor, occurrence context, and encoding set. Entries are intentionally semantic-specific; they do not create a semantics × maximum-depth cross-product. Seller-wide capabilities are only a ceiling and the selected product format option is binding.

verifier_constraints.adcp_semantic_identity: when dialect is adcp, dialect_semantic must equal universal_semantic
verifier_constraints.translation_chain: a translate_to_native entry is usable only when the same capability set contains an exact resolve_value entry for translation_target

locale_policy.title: Creative Locale Policy
locale_policy.description: Seller-declared locale eligibility for one product or placement format declaration. Each accepted_language_ranges entry is a concrete canonical BCP 47 language range evaluated with RFC 4647 section 3.3.1 Basic Filtering: fr accepts fr, fr-CA, and fr-FR, while fr-CA accepts only fr-CA and its more-specific descendants. Ranges are ORed and wildcards are not supported. Presence is a hard assignment constraint, not a preference: at least one materialized creative locale variant must match. The seller filters the creative to eligible variants before applying buyer-declared strict Lookup, locale_fallbacks, or default behavior; buyer policy can never select a seller-ineligible variant.

accepted_language_ranges.description: Concrete canonical BCP 47 language ranges accepted by this format option. RFC 4647 Basic Filtering is directional: seller range fr accepts variant fr-CA, but seller range fr-CA does not accept variant fr or fr-FR. Use zxx explicitly for language-neutral creative; und means unknown and is not a wildcard.

items.title: Language Tag
items.description: A well-formed BCP 47 language tag used by AdCP only as language identity. Script and region may refine that identity; other valid BCP 47 subtags remain part of tag matching but do not make this a general locale-settings object. It does not determine currency, time zone, number/date formatting, market, or legal jurisdiction. The AdCP canonical wire profile requires lower-case language and variants, title-case script, and upper-case region (for example `en-US`, `zh-Hant-TW`, or `x-private`). RFC 5646 comparisons are case-insensitive and its case regularization is optional; AdCP intentionally requires this stricter single wire spelling and receivers MUST reject differently cased tags rather than silently normalizing them. The schema pattern enforces the AdCP casing profile and extension structure for commonly used tags; conforming receivers additionally validate the complete RFC 5646 grammar and registry rules. Every new AdCP field carrying BCP 47 language identity or a concrete language range MUST reference this schema instead of declaring independent string constraints.

format_schema.title: Platform Extension Reference
format_schema.description:
Reference to a platform extension definition. The agent that owns the URI is authoritative for the extension's schema. Buyers fetch the definition once per content digest and cache it. Platform extensions are typically bundled in `get_products` responses under an `extensions` map keyed by `uri@digest`, eliminating the need for a separate fetch.

**Within a single response**, multiple references to the same `uri` MUST carry the same `digest` — divergent digests in one response indicate producer-side error (e.g., concurrent extension revision mid-render). Buyers encountering divergent digests for the same URI MUST fail closed: treat all references to that URI as unresolved and surface a validation error rather than picking one branch silently. **Across responses**, digest divergence is normal — extension authors revise their schemas, the new digest differs, the cache key changes, and the buyer refetches. Cache by `uri@digest`, not by `uri` alone.

uri.description: HTTPS URL identifying the extension. `https://` is mandatory — `http://`, `file://`, `data:`, and other schemes are rejected at the schema layer (defense-in-depth on top of the fetch-contract normative rules). The URI base is the owning agent's URL; the path identifies the extension within that agent. The full fetch contract — SSRF allowlist, response-size cap, $ref sandbox, schema-compile bounds — is documented on `product-format-declaration.json#format_schema` and applies to ALL fetches of this reference shape. Referenced platform extensions carry acceptance narrowing and MUST NOT be discarded as informational metadata. Without a verified cached, bundled, or fetched body, the affected declaration remains unresolved; buyers MUST NOT claim compatibility against a weakened contract with that narrowing removed. Other independently resolved declarations remain usable, or buyers may obtain authoritative seller validation of the complete effective contract, including the unresolved extension.

digest.description: SHA-256 content digest of the extension definition (sha256:<hex>). Used to detect drift — if the agent revises the extension, the digest changes and cached definitions become invalid.

canonical_params.custom: validate params against fetched format_schema uri and digest

allOf.description: Shared DAAST tracker vocabulary and execution-selector constraints. The legacy asset vocabulary retains AdCP's historical close extension, while the closed standards selector matrix excludes it. Progress alone carries offset in selectors.

Existing 3.x asset schemas remain structurally permissive; the selector schema supplies the closed event/target matrix for contract matching.
x-adcp-validation.format_slot_satisfiability: Every asset_type named by honored MUST have at least one matching first-class slot in the effective selected canonical format declaration. A contract cannot promise execution for an asset shape that the same format rejects structurally.
x-adcp-validation.layer_derivation: Publisher, placement, and seller effective-contract derivation is evaluated over atomic tuples of normalized non-version selector identity, one exact version (or null for pixel), execution_actor, and one firing_path. For a complete parent, every child tuple MUST exist in the parent, the child remains complete, and array compression MUST NOT create a version/path cross-product. An incomplete or omitted parent is not a ceiling: a child may add or omit affirmative tuples for its narrower scope, but remains incomplete until every applicable layer is complete. Omission from an incomplete child is undeclared, not an assertion that the tuple is unsupported.
x-adcp-validation.cardinality: Each accepted manifest tracker instance is initiated exactly once in total for each logical event occurrence; identical URLs are not deduplicated.

enumDescriptions.AXEM: AXE contextual metadata (encoded blob). Legacy — in TMP, use Offer creative_data for dynamic creative values and TMPX for exposure tracking.
enumDescriptions.CATALOG_ID: Buyer-defined catalog identifier from the catalog's catalog_id field
enumDescriptions.SKU: Product SKU identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.GTIN: Global Trade Item Number for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OFFERING_ID: AdCP offering identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.JOB_ID: Job posting identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.HOTEL_ID: Hotel property identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.FLIGHT_ID: Flight route identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.VEHICLE_ID: Vehicle listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.LISTING_ID: Real estate listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.STORE_ID: Store location identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.PROGRAM_ID: Education program identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.DESTINATION_ID: Travel destination identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.CREATIVE_VARIANT_ID: Seller-assigned creative variant identifier, passed through at serve time
enumDescriptions.APP_ITEM_ID: Mobile app identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.ITEM_NAME: Name/title of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: name). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_DESCRIPTION: Description of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: description). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_TAGLINE: Short promotional tagline of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: tagline). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE: Price amount of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.amount). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE_CURRENCY: ISO 4217 currency code of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.currency). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.

macro_resolution_capabilities.description: Binding format-option processing capabilities for exact macro dialect identities, semantics, operations, actors, contexts, and encodings. Absence means undeclared, not supported on the opt-in declared-token path. Seller-wide capabilities are only a ceiling. This field does not claim that a buyer tracker asset is honored or fired.

verifier_constraints.translation_chain_closure: every translate_to_native entry must have an exact matching resolve_value entry for its translation_target in this same array

technical_requirements_complete.description: When true, every technical creative-acceptance constraint for this declaration layer is expressed and omitted technical fields mean no constraint. When false or absent, omitted technical fields are undeclared and MUST NOT be inferred. The effective contract is complete only when every applicable declaration layer asserts true.

locale_policy.title: Creative Locale Policy
locale_policy.description: Seller-declared locale eligibility for one product or placement format declaration. Each accepted_language_ranges entry is a concrete canonical BCP 47 language range evaluated with RFC 4647 section 3.3.1 Basic Filtering: fr accepts fr, fr-CA, and fr-FR, while fr-CA accepts only fr-CA and its more-specific descendants. Ranges are ORed and wildcards are not supported. Presence is a hard assignment constraint, not a preference: at least one materialized creative locale variant must match. The seller filters the creative to eligible variants before applying buyer-declared strict Lookup, locale_fallbacks, or default behavior; buyer policy can never select a seller-ineligible variant.

accepted_language_ranges.description: Concrete canonical BCP 47 language ranges accepted by this format option. RFC 4647 Basic Filtering is directional: seller range fr accepts variant fr-CA, but seller range fr-CA does not accept variant fr or fr-FR. Use zxx explicitly for language-neutral creative; und means unknown and is not a wildcard.

items.title: Language Tag
items.description: A well-formed BCP 47 language tag used by AdCP only as language identity. Script and region may refine that identity; other valid BCP 47 subtags remain part of tag matching but do not make this a general locale-settings object. It does not determine currency, time zone, number/date formatting, market, or legal jurisdiction. The AdCP canonical wire profile requires lower-case language and variants, title-case script, and upper-case region (for example `en-US`, `zh-Hant-TW`, or `x-private`). RFC 5646 comparisons are case-insensitive and its case regularization is optional; AdCP intentionally requires this stricter single wire spelling and receivers MUST reject differently cased tags rather than silently normalizing them. The schema pattern enforces the AdCP casing profile and extension structure for commonly used tags; conforming receivers additionally validate the complete RFC 5646 grammar and registry rules. Every new AdCP field carrying BCP 47 language identity or a concrete language range MUST reference this schema instead of declaring independent string constraints.

format_kind.$comment: Keep this enum inline for SDK code generation; tracker-execution-package-integration.test.cjs checks exact parity with canonical-format-kind.json.

format_schema.title: Platform Extension Reference
format_schema.description:
Reference to a platform extension definition. The agent that owns the URI is authoritative for the extension's schema. Buyers fetch the definition once per content digest and cache it. Platform extensions are typically bundled in `get_products` responses under an `extensions` map keyed by `uri@digest`, eliminating the need for a separate fetch.

**Within a single response**, multiple references to the same `uri` MUST carry the same `digest` — divergent digests in one response indicate producer-side error (e.g., concurrent extension revision mid-render). Buyers encountering divergent digests for the same URI MUST fail closed: treat all references to that URI as unresolved and surface a validation error rather than picking one branch silently. **Across responses**, digest divergence is normal — extension authors revise their schemas, the new digest differs, the cache key changes, and the buyer refetches. Cache by `uri@digest`, not by `uri` alone.

uri.description: HTTPS URL identifying the extension. `https://` is mandatory — `http://`, `file://`, `data:`, and other schemes are rejected at the schema layer (defense-in-depth on top of the fetch-contract normative rules). The URI base is the owning agent's URL; the path identifies the extension within that agent. The full fetch contract — SSRF allowlist, response-size cap, $ref sandbox, schema-compile bounds — is documented on `product-format-declaration.json#format_schema` and applies to ALL fetches of this reference shape. Referenced platform extensions carry acceptance narrowing and MUST NOT be discarded as informational metadata. Without a verified cached, bundled, or fetched body, the affected declaration remains unresolved; buyers MUST NOT claim compatibility against a weakened contract with that narrowing removed. Other independently resolved declarations remain usable, or buyers may obtain authoritative seller validation of the complete effective contract, including the unresolved extension.

digest.description: SHA-256 content digest of the extension definition (sha256:<hex>). Used to detect drift — if the agent revises the extension, the digest changes and cached definitions become invalid.

canonical_params.custom: validate params against fetched format_schema uri and digest

identifiers.description: Optional external inventory identifiers for this placement. Externally governed values should be authority-prefixed; seller-local values are scoped by the surrounding publisher namespace. For publisher_ref placements, the effective set is the union of publisher and product declarations, de-duplicated by exact (type, value).

type.title: Property Identifier Types
type.description: Valid identifier types for property and placement identification across different media types

enumDescriptions.screen_id: DOOH screen identifier within a venue
enumDescriptions.openooh_venue_type: OpenOOH Venue Taxonomy enumeration ID, prefixed with the taxonomy authority and version for unambiguous interchange (for example openooh-1.1:20501 for Retail / Malls / Concourse). Bare or dotted hierarchy values are ambiguous and SHOULD NOT be emitted by new senders.
enumDescriptions.rss_url: RSS feed URL for podcast or content feed
enumDescriptions.station_id: Broadcast station identifier — call sign, station name, or other locally recognized identifier (e.g., WCBS-FM, BBC Radio 4, France Inter, 2GB)
enumDescriptions.facility_id: Broadcast facility or license ID from a national regulator, prefixed with authority slug (e.g., fcc:73953, ofcom:AL000001). Known prefixes: fcc (US), crtc (Canada), ift (Mexico), ofcom (UK), arcom (France), bnetza/medienanstalt (Germany), acma (Australia), mic (Japan), kcc (South Korea), anatel (Brazil), enacom (Argentina), trai (India)

collections.description: A non-empty array is the complete roster. `[]` means undisclosed. MUST NOT be `[]` below 3.3. Each entry references collections declared in an adagents.json by domain and explicit collection_ids. Full collection objects arrive in the response's top-level collections array when the request sets include_collections and the seller supports it (experimental, media_buy.collection_cards); otherwise buyers resolve them from the referenced adagents.json, which remains the authorization source either way. The domain-only bulk-grant selector form is for authorization scoping, not product composition. A selected-mode collection_selection names collections from this set.

allOf.title: Collection Selector
allOf.description: References collections declared in an adagents.json, keyed by (publisher_domain, collection_id). The publisher's adagents.json at the given domain is the authoritative declaration and the root of authorization. Buyers can also get a selling agent's copy of each referenced collection: in the top-level collections array of a product or proposal response requested with include_collections, or from list_collections (both experimental). Those copies follow core/response-collection.json: they win only on a closed list of display fields and are never authorization evidence, and any collection a seller omits resolves from adagents.json. When collection_ids is omitted, the selector references every collection declared in that adagents.json — the bulk-grant form for authorization scoping (e.g., a host authorizing a channel owner's sales agent for all of the owner's collections without tracking owner-assigned IDs).

publisher_domain.description: Domain where the adagents.json declaring these collections is hosted (e.g., 'mrbeast.com'). The collections array in that file contains the authoritative collection definitions.

collection_ids.description: Collection IDs from the adagents.json collections array. Each ID must match a collection_id declared in that file. Omit to reference all collections declared in that file.

collection_targeting_allowed.description: Whether buyers can select a subset of this product's collections through targeting_overlay.collection_list, collection_lists, or collection_selection. When false, the product is a fixed bundle (a collection_selection that exactly restates the complete bundle remains an inherent match).

installments.description: Specific installments this product includes — the episodes, issues, airings, rotation periods, or creator slots being sold. Each entry names its parent through the canonical collection_ref tuple; unlike the legacy get_products installment there is no publisher-domain-free shorthand. Every referenced collection MUST be one the product's collections selectors name, so collections is required alongside. Absence is meaningful within a projection that requested this field, and is not 'no installments known': a product that carries collections and omits installments is run-of-collection — inventory across those collections, whatever publishes during the flight. Absence from a list_products response whose fields projection did not request installments carries no meaning at all, which is why a buyer that depends on the run-of-collection reading MUST request the field explicitly. Buyers MUST reject a product whose installment collection_ref is not one its own collections selectors name; the seller's collections are what the referenced adagents.json authorizes.

items.title: Canonical Installment
items.description: Compact closed installment view for the AdCP compact product lifecycle — one episode, issue, event, rotation period, or creator slot within a collection. Identity is the tuple (collection_ref, installment_id), so both fields are required and the deprecated publisher-domain-free collection_id shorthand carried by the legacy get_products installment is absent. The parent collection's kind indicates how to interpret each installment. Installments inherit collection-level fields they don't override: content_rating defaults to the collection's baseline, guest_talent is additive to the collection's recurring talent, and topics add context beyond the collection's genre.

installment_id.description: Installment ID within the referenced collection. Collection-scoped, not globally unique.

collection_ref.title: Collection Reference
collection_ref.description: Canonical parent collection identity. Required: the canonical surface has no single-namespace shorthand, so every installment names the publisher domain and collection ID that scope its installment_id. The referenced collection MUST be one the enclosing product's collections selectors name.

publisher_domain.description: Domain where the adagents.json declaring this collection is hosted.

collection_id.description: Collection ID from the publisher's adagents.json collection catalog.

scheduled_at.description: When the installment airs or publishes (ISO 8601)

enumDescriptions.tentative: May not happen (e.g., playoff Game 7 depends on Game 6)
enumDescriptions.live: Currently airing or streaming right now
enumDescriptions.postponed: Was scheduled but delayed to a future date

duration_seconds.description: Expected duration of the installment in seconds

flexible_end.description: Whether the end time is approximate (live events, sports)

valid_until.description: When this installment data expires and should be re-queried. Buyers should re-query before committing budget to a product with tentative installments.

content_rating.title: Content Rating
content_rating.description: Installment-specific content rating. Overrides the collection's baseline content_rating when present.

topics.description: Content topics for this installment. Uses the same taxonomy as the collection's genre_taxonomy when present. Enables installment-level brand safety evaluation beyond content_rating.

special.title: Special
special.description: Installment-specific event context. When present, this installment is anchored to a real-world event. Overrides the collection-level special when present.

name.description: Name of the event (e.g., 'Olympics 2028', 'Super Bowl LXI')

ends.description: When the event ends (ISO 8601). Omit for single-day events.

guest_talent.description: Installment-specific guests and talent. Additive to the collection's recurring talent.

items.title: Talent
items.description: A person associated with a collection or installment, with an optional link to their brand.json identity

name.description: Person's name as credited on the collection

brand_ref.title: Brand Reference
brand_ref.description: Experimental (media_buy.collection_cards). Typed link to this person's brand in brand.json, for example a rights-holder brand with right_type talent. When brand_ref and brand_url are both present they MUST identify the same brand (brand_url's host equals brand_ref.domain), and brand_ref wins. Only domain and brand_id are read here; other brand_ref fields are ignored. The link is one-sided: buyers SHOULD treat it as confirmed only when that brand's get_brand_identity collections lists the same {publisher_domain, collection_id} back.

domain.description: Domain where /.well-known/brand.json is hosted, or the brand's operating domain

brand_id.title: Brand ID
brand_id.description: Brand within a brand.json that lists several brands. Optional for single-brand domains.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries the advertiser account serves. This is an account attribute: it does not identify the brand or the account, and it is not delivery targeting. Omit when the account is not limited to particular countries. Array order is not meaningful.

industries.description: Inline override for the brand's industries. Useful when the caller cannot modify the brand's canonical brand.json but needs to declare industries for governance (e.g., Annex III vertical detection). brand.json remains the canonical source; when omitted here, governance agents SHOULD resolve from brand.json.

data_subject_contestation.description: Inline override for the brand's contestation contact point. Useful when the operator does not control brand.json but needs to discharge Art 22(3) for this plan. brand.json is canonical; when omitted, governance agents resolve brand → house → missing.

brand_kit_override.description:
Inline override for brand-kit fields normally resolved from `/.well-known/brand.json` on `domain` (logo, colors, voice, tagline). Use when brand.json is missing, stale, or inappropriate for this specific call — e.g., a campaign-scoped tagline, a co-branded creative, a freshly-rebranded color palette the brand.json hasn't shipped yet. Same inline-override pattern as `industries` and `data_subject_contestation` above: brand.json is canonical, the override is per-call. Adopters needing to override fields outside this subset MUST publish a different brand.json and reference it via a different `domain` — the inline override is intentionally narrow to a small high-traffic subset. The brand-wide `prohibited_terms` list is one such field: it lives on brand.json and has no per-call override.

**Merge semantics (normative).** The merge is **field-level**, not whole-object replacement. Each field within `brand_kit_override` (`logo`, `colors`, `voice`, `tagline`) is evaluated independently — when a field is present on the override the override value applies; when a field is absent the brand.json value applies (or is absent if brand.json doesn't carry one either). For composite fields (`colors.primary`, `colors.secondary`, `colors.accent`), the merge is one level deeper: each color slot is evaluated independently — a producer can override `colors.primary` while still inheriting `colors.secondary` from brand.json. SDKs MUST NOT treat a present `brand_kit_override.colors` as wiping the brand.json `colors` block entirely; only the per-slot fields present in the override take precedence. Without this rule, a partial-override semantics would diverge across SDKs and produce inconsistent rendering for the same payload.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as an image asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

file_size_bytes.description: Image file size in bytes. Required by agents that advertise a max_file_size_kb constraint.

pixel_ratio.description: Intrinsic pixels per logical render pixel (for example `2` for a 600×500 image intended to render at 300×250). Optional because a validator can infer the ratio when the target format declares logical dimensions. When supplied, it MUST agree with both `width / logical_width` and `height / logical_height`; it is never a substitute for the intrinsic `width` and `height` fields.

state_id.description: Binding used only when this image populates a `seller_rendered_stateful_display` `state_canvases` slot. It MUST match one declared `states[].state_id` (semantic validators resolve it). Omit for ordinary image slots.

breakpoint_id.description: Binding used only when this image populates a `seller_rendered_stateful_display` `state_canvases` slot. It MUST match one breakpoint declared on the selected state (semantic validators resolve it). Omit for ordinary image slots.

focal_point.description: Normalized `[x, y]` coordinates (0–1 from top-left) of the image's visual anchor. Seller-side renderers crop toward the focal point when deriving renditions across breakpoints and aspect ratios; absent, cropping falls back to center-weighted defaults.

format.description: Image file format (jpg, png, gif, webp, etc.)

provenance.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

voice.description: Override brand-voice description for surface-composed text/audio output.

brand_url.description: URL to this person's brand.json entry. Enables buyer agents to evaluate the talent's brand identity and associations.

ad_inventory.title: Ad Inventory Configuration
ad_inventory.description: Break-based ad inventory for this installment. For non-break formats (host reads, integrations), use the product's placements.

expected_breaks.description: Number of planned ad breaks in the installment

total_ad_seconds.description: Total seconds of ad time across all breaks

max_ad_duration_seconds.description: Maximum duration in seconds for a single ad within a break. Buyers need this to know whether their creative fits.

unplanned_breaks.description: Whether ad breaks are dynamic and driven by live conditions (sports timeouts, election coverage). When false, all breaks are pre-defined.

supported_formats.description: Ad format types supported in breaks (e.g., 'video', 'audio', 'display')

deadlines.title: Installment Deadlines
deadlines.description: Booking, cancellation, and material submission deadlines for this installment. Present when the installment has time-sensitive inventory that requires advance commitment or material delivery.

booking_deadline.description: Last date/time to book a placement in this installment (ISO 8601). After this point, the seller will not accept new bookings.

cancellation_deadline.description: Last date/time to cancel without penalty (ISO 8601). Cancellations after this point may incur fees per the seller's terms.

change_cutoff.description: Last date/time at which a change to or stop of this installment (creative swap, pause, cancellation instruction) still takes operational effect: broadcast traffic/log close, OOH posting-cycle lock, print issue close, cinema reel lock. Distinct from `cancellation_deadline` (penalty-free cancel window; a cancellation after `change_cutoff` may still be billed even if within terms) and `booking_deadline` (new bookings). When both are present, `change_cutoff` SHOULD NOT precede `booking_deadline`. Absent means the seller makes no statement.

material_deadlines.description: Stages for creative material submission. Items MUST be in chronological order by due_at (earliest first). Typical pattern: 'draft' for raw materials the seller will process, 'final' for production-ready assets. Print example: draft artwork then press-ready PDF. Influencer example: talking points then approved script.

items.title: Material Deadline
items.description: A deadline for creative material submission. Sellers declare stages to distinguish draft materials (e.g., talking points, raw artwork) from production-ready assets (e.g., approved scripts, press-ready PDFs).

stage.description: Submission stage identifier. Use 'draft' for materials that need seller processing and 'final' for production-ready assets. Sellers may define additional stages.

due_at.description: When materials for this stage are due (ISO 8601)

label.description: What the seller needs at this stage (e.g., 'Talking points and brand guidelines', 'Press-ready PDF with bleed')

derivative_of.title: Canonical Installment Derivation
derivative_of.description: When this installment is a clip, highlight, or recap derived from a full installment. Unlike the legacy form, the source is a canonical installment_ref, so a derivative may name a source in another collection.

installment_ref.title: Canonical Installment Reference
installment_ref.description: The source installment this content is derived from.

collection_ref.title: Canonical Collection Reference
collection_ref.description: Closed parent collection identity. Collection IDs are scoped to the adagents.json at publisher_domain, so both members participate in identity.

installment_id.description: Installment ID within the referenced collection.

type.title: Derivative Type
type.description: What kind of derivative content this is

enumDescriptions.clip: Short excerpt from the source installment
enumDescriptions.highlight: Editorially curated best-of segment from the source installment
enumDescriptions.recap: Summary of the source installment's content
enumDescriptions.trailer: Promotional content for the source installment
enumDescriptions.bonus: Supplementary content (behind-the-scenes, extended interviews, deleted segments)

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

enumDescriptions.non_guaranteed: Inventory without reserved or guaranteed delivery, commonly auction-based or otherwise best-effort. Do not use for scheduled broadcast buys solely because final audience delivery is estimated from historical ranges or settles through third-party measurement.

exclusivity.title: Exclusivity
exclusivity.description: Whether a product offers exclusive access to its inventory

enumDescriptions.none: No exclusivity — multiple advertisers can buy this product simultaneously
enumDescriptions.category: Category-exclusive — only one advertiser per industry category (e.g., one auto brand per collection sponsorship)
enumDescriptions.exclusive: Sole sponsorship — only one advertiser can buy this product

items.title: Canonical Pricing Option
items.description: Self-contained selected pricing terms for compact product offers and accepted commercial snapshots. Deprecated execution hints such as max_bid are absent; bidding intent lives in BiddingPolicy.

price_guidance.title: Price Guidance
price_guidance.description: Pricing guidance for auction-based bidding. Helps buyers calibrate bids with historical percentiles.

price_breakdown.title: Price Breakdown
price_breakdown.description: Breaks down how the buyer's effective price is composed from list_price. Adjustment kinds: fee and operator_fee increase the price, discount reduces it, and commission and settlement are disclosed without changing it. Invariant: list_price with fee, discount, and operator_fee adjustments applied in array order, rounded to currency precision at each step (or to the option's price precision when it declares price_adjustments, see price-adjustments.json, which can be finer), equals fixed_price when the parent object carries it; on auction-based packages the breakdown is informational. Sellers never emit operator_fee. The operator's buying platform adds it after every fee and discount; the running price before the first operator_fee is the seller's price, to which commission and settlement apply. Budgets are denominated at fixed_price, inclusive of commissions; a buying platform's budget toward the advertiser also includes operator fees.

list_price.description: Rate card or base price before any adjustments. The starting point from which fixed_price is derived by applying fee, discount, and operator_fee adjustments sequentially.

adjustments.description: Ordered list of price adjustments. Fee, discount, and operator_fee adjustments walk list_price to the buyer's effective price — fees and operator fees increase the running price, discounts reduce it. Commission and settlement adjustments are disclosed for transparency but do not affect the buyer's committed price.

name.description: Specific adjustment name. Use well-known values where applicable for interoperability.

rate.description: Adjustment as a decimal proportion (e.g., 0.15 for 15%). Always positive — kind determines the economic effect. Mutually exclusive with amount.

amount.description: Adjustment as a fixed monetary amount in the pricing option's currency. Always positive — kind determines the economic effect. Mutually exclusive with rate.

description.description: Human-readable description of this adjustment (e.g., 'Malstaffel 12x', '2% Skonto 10 Tage')

beneficiary.description: Identifies who receives this adjustment's value. For commissions, the intermediary (e.g., a sellers.json domain, an AdCP account ID, or a human-readable party name). Optional but recommended for multi-intermediary transparency. For operator_fee, defaults to the account's operator; set it only when another party, such as the buying platform, receives the fee.

forecast.title: Canonical Delivery Forecast
forecast.description: Compact product forecast without legacy BrandRef or creative dependencies.

items.title: Canonical Forecast Point
items.description: Compact forecast row with numeric ranges and identity-only measurement-vendor references.

dimensions.title: Forecast Point Dimensions
dimensions.description: Dimension constraints represented by a ForecastPoint. Use this when one product, proposal, or signal coverage forecast needs to expose availability or forecasted delivery by country, region, placement, device, audience, signal value, time window, or intersections such as placement x country without creating separate products solely for each slice. Each item declares one dimension family via `kind`; when multiple items are present, the point represents their intersection. Sellers MUST NOT emit more than one item for each `kind` in a point. Consumers MUST NOT treat repeated kinds as OR semantics; repeated peer values such as two countries are a seller conformance issue. Dimension values are descriptors of the forecast row and are independent of pricing_options.

x-adcp-validation.description: `dimensions[]` is an array for readable intersection syntax, but `kind` is a logical set key. JSON Schema draft-07 cannot express unique-by-property for this array shape, so conformance tooling should reject repeated `kind` values.

oneOf.title: Geo Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: A geographic dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

geo_level.title: Geographic Targeting Level
geo_level.description: Geographic level for this forecast point.

system.description: Classification system for metro or postal_area levels. Required when geo_level is 'metro' or 'postal_area'. Metro rows use metro-system enum values such as 'nielsen_dma'; native postal rows use country-local postal-system enum values such as 'zip' with country 'US'; deprecated legacy postal rows may use legacy-postal-system enum values such as 'us_zip'. Omit for country and region rows.

country.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code. Required for native postal_area rows and omitted for legacy postal rows, metro rows, country rows, and region rows.

geo_code.description: Geographic code within the level and system. Country: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 ('US'). Region: ISO 3166-2 with country prefix ('US-CA'). Metro/postal: system-specific code ('501', '10001').

geo_name.description: Human-readable geographic name (e.g., 'United States', 'California', 'New York DMA').

anyOf.title: Postal Country System
anyOf.description: Valid country-local postal system pairing. Registered countries only accept their registered local systems; countries without a registered local system use postal_code or custom.

oneOf.title: Placement Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: A placement dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

placement_ref.title: Placement Reference
placement_ref.description: Structured placement reference for this forecast row. References an entry from the product's placements array.

publisher_domain.description: Domain where the adagents.json declaring a publisher-catalog placement is hosted, or the inventory publisher associated with an inline placement. Omitted only for legacy single-publisher product-context references.

placement_id.description: Placement ID from the publisher's adagents.json placement catalog, or an inline seller-defined placement ID interpreted within the enclosing seller and product context.

placement_name.description: Human-readable placement name, useful when the buyer has not resolved the placement catalog.

oneOf.title: Device Type Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: A device form-factor dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

device_type.title: Device Type
device_type.description: Device form factor for this forecast row.

oneOf.title: Device Platform Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: An operating-system or platform dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

device_platform.title: Device Platform
device_platform.description: Operating system or platform for this forecast row.

oneOf.title: Audience Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: An audience segment dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

audience_id.description: Audience segment identifier for this forecast row.

oneOf.title: Signal Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: A signal value or signal-presence dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules.

signal_ref.title: Signal Ref
signal_ref.description: Canonical signal reference for this forecast row. Required when the row needs to disambiguate product-local, data-provider, or signal-source identity. Product-relative forecasts SHOULD use signal_ref.

oneOf.description: Product-scoped signal. oneOf.title: Time Forecast Dimension
oneOf.description: A calendar-window dimension for a ForecastPoint row. Variant of ForecastPoint dimensions; see forecast-point-dimensions.json for dispatch rules. Windows are half-open intervals [start_time, end_time): the row covers instants at or after start_time and strictly before end_time, so adjacent windows share a boundary without overlapping. end_time MUST be after start_time; JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare sibling values, so conformance tooling enforces the ordering. Within one forecast, sellers MUST emit non-overlapping windows and SHOULD coalesce adjacent windows whose availability_status and metrics do not materially differ. When the request scoped the forecast with offer_filters.availability_horizon, a complete forecast partitions the requested horizon; a seller that cannot cover the full horizon signals the gap through the response's incomplete[] mechanism rather than silently omitting windows.

start_time.description: Inclusive window start (RFC 3339 date-time with timezone offset).

end_time.description: Exclusive window end (RFC 3339 date-time with timezone offset). MUST be after start_time.

enumDescriptions.available: The inventory described by this row can be booked as of generated_at. This is a snapshot, not a reservation — another buyer can take the window before this buyer commits.
enumDescriptions.unavailable: The inventory described by this row cannot be booked. Rows may carry empty metrics. Sellers MUST NOT disclose who holds a conflicting booking.

supports_demographic_breakdown.description: Product-scoped demographic breakdown capability. Reporting capability is independent of demographic targeting capability: a product can execute an exact buyer age predicate while its measurement source reports only fixed age intervals. Buyers compare requested reporting ranges with this declaration before requesting by_demographic rows and MUST NOT infer reporting alignment from Product.demographic_targeting.

age.description: Machine-comparable age ranges this product can report.

reporting_modes.description: Ways this product can produce age rows. exact_predicates accepts requested canonical age predicates within the declared bounds. enumerated_intervals reports only the exact intervals declared in intervals; buyers may aggregate adjacent complete intervals but MUST NOT treat a wider or narrower interval as the requested audience.

min_reportable_age.description: Lowest explicit min or max bound accepted by exact_predicates. Required when that mode is declared.

max_reportable_age.description: Highest explicit min or max bound accepted by exact_predicates. Required when that mode is declared.

supports_unbounded_min.description: Whether exact_predicates accepts a canonical age predicate with min omitted. Required when that mode is declared.

supports_unbounded_max.description: Whether exact_predicates accepts a canonical age predicate with max omitted. Required when that mode is declared.

intervals.description: Fixed reportable age intervals for enumerated_intervals. Bounds are authoritative capability data, not a protocol-wide bucket taxonomy. Optional native labels identify the measurement-system code returned with the interval.

age.title: Demographic Age Range
age.description: A canonical audience-age predicate in completed integer years. min and max are inclusive; omitting one bound means no restriction in that direction. At least one bound is required. include_unknown is always explicit because people whose age is unavailable are not members of any numeric interval. Implementations MUST reject min greater than max; JSON Schema draft-07 cannot compare sibling numeric values.

min.description: Inclusive minimum age in completed years. Omit for an open lower bound.

max.description: Inclusive maximum age in completed years. Omit for an open upper bound.

include_unknown.description: Whether delivery to people whose age is unavailable is part of this predicate. This field has no default and MUST be supplied.

demographic.description: Optional native demographic label returned for this interval.

demographic_systems.description: Measurement-system notations this product may return. A code remains opaque unless its capability interval and response row also carry a canonical age predicate.

may_suppress_small_cells.description: Whether privacy, policy, or measurement thresholds may suppress otherwise reportable demographic rows. When true, buyers must inspect by_demographic_suppressed before testing whether rows reconcile to package totals.

supports_spot_breakdown.description: Product-scoped spot-level as-run reporting capability. Presence means the seller can report stable spot identities and actual airing timestamps. available_metrics declares which delivery metrics may eventually be populated at spot grain; an empty array means the product provides airing evidence only. available_statuses and supports_break_position are experimental in AdCP 3.3 and tell the buyer which spot lifecycle and break-position fields the seller populates, so a missing row or field is not mistaken for non-delivery.

available_metrics.description: Metrics available at spot grain. A declared metric may be absent from a provisional measurement window and appear when a later window supersedes it. A metric omitted from this declaration is not promised at spot grain even when it is available at package grain.

available_statuses.description: Spot lifecycle statuses this product reports in by_spot. Absent, or an empty array, means the seller reports only aired rows without a spot_status, the AdCP 3.2 behavior. When present, a status that is not listed is not reported: the absence of scheduled, preempted, or makegood rows then proves nothing about whether any such spots exist, and a buyer MUST NOT read it as nothing scheduled, nothing preempted, or no makegoods. 'aired' is always reported and need not be listed. Sellers MUST NOT emit this field to callers pinned below AdCP 3.3, or to callers with no declared pin.

items.title: Spot Status
items.description: Lifecycle status of a by_spot row. Experimental in AdCP 3.3. A spot_id moves scheduled → aired or scheduled → preempted; a makegood is a separate row, with its own spot_id, that replaces a preempted spot.

enumDescriptions.scheduled: Planned but not yet aired. The seller may still move or preempt the spot. The row carries scheduled_at and no aired_at; any delivery metrics are expectations, not actuals.
enumDescriptions.aired: Aired. The row carries aired_at. This is the implied status when spot_status is absent.
enumDescriptions.preempted: Was scheduled and did not air. The row carries scheduled_at (the slot that was lost) and no aired_at.
enumDescriptions.makegood: Aired as a replacement for a preempted spot. The row carries aired_at and replaces_spot_id.

supports_break_position.description: Whether the seller populates break_position on by_spot rows. When false or absent, a row without break_position means the position is not reported, not that the spot ran outside a commercial break. Sellers MUST NOT emit this field to callers pinned below AdCP 3.3, or to callers with no declared pin.

items.title: Measurement Window
items.description: A measurement maturation stage for any channel where billing-grade data is produced in phases rather than arriving final on day one. Each window represents an accumulation or processing stage with its own expected availability. Examples: broadcast/linear TV (live → C3 → C7 DVR accumulation), DOOH (tentative plays → post-IVT/fraud-check final), digital (raw impressions → GIVT filtered → SIVT filtered), podcast (7-day downloads → 30-day downloads), audio/radio (tentative → diary/panel-certified). Sellers whose data is final on first delivery omit this.

window_id.description: Identifier for this maturation stage. Standard broadcast values: 'live' (real-time viewers only), 'c3' (live + 3 days time-shifted), 'c7' (live + 7 days time-shifted). Standard values for other channels include 'tentative' (provisional data available quickly), 'final' (post-processing certified data), 'post_ivt' (digital after invalid-traffic filtering), 'post_sivt' (digital after sophisticated-IVT filtering), 'downloads_7d' / 'downloads_30d' (podcast download maturation). Sellers may define custom IDs.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this window measures
examples: Live plus 7 days of time-shifted viewing
Tentative plays before IVT and fraud-check processing
Final plays after IVT and fraud-check processing

duration_days.description: Number of days of accumulation included in this window before processing begins. For broadcast, this is DVR accumulation (0 = live only, 3 = live + 3 days DVR, 7 = live + 7 days DVR). For channels without an accumulation period (DOOH tentative→final, digital IVT filtering), this is 0 — maturation is entirely vendor processing time captured in expected_availability_days.

expected_availability_days.description: Expected number of days after delivery before this window's data is available from the measurement vendor. Captures accumulation time plus vendor processing time. Examples: broadcast C7 from VideoAmp ~22 days (7-day accumulation + ~15-day processing); DOOH tentative plays same-day; DOOH final (post-IVT/fraud-check) ~1 day; digital post-SIVT ~2–3 days.

is_guarantee_basis.description: Whether this window is the basis for delivery guarantees, reconciliation, and invoicing. A product typically has one guarantee basis window (e.g., C7 for most US broadcast, post-IVT final for DOOH). Buyers reconcile against the guarantee basis window's final numbers.

signal_targeting_rules.title: Signal Targeting Rules
signal_targeting_rules.description: Product-level composition rules for selecting signals on packages. The selectable signal menu may come from inline signal_targeting_options or from get_signals for wholesale signal discovery when the product omits inline options. These rules are intentionally product-scoped, not seller-level get_adcp_capabilities, because a single seller may route products through different ad servers with different signal targeting limits. Sellers MUST echo the applied signal_targeting_groups on the resulting package state, including fixed/default selections the seller applies without buyer edits.

resolution_model.description: How selected signal_targeting_options are resolved against the product's inventory. 'direct_targeting' means selected signals are applied as targeting predicates to the package inventory. 'seller_planned' means selected signals are planning inputs that the seller resolves against product-specific inventory, timing, availability, reach, or pacing constraints; buyers SHOULD NOT attempt to decompose the signal selection into lower-level inventory or schedule decisions. Use 'seller_planned' for products such as linear broadcast schedules where the audience definition may be portable but the audience-to-avails plan is seller-resolved.

selection_mode.description: Default selection behavior for selectable signals on this product. 'optional' means the buyer may select zero or more signals. 'required' means the buyer must select at least min_selected_signals, or 1 when min_selected_signals is omitted. 'fixed' means the seller applies the default_selected signals and the buyer cannot add or remove them; buyers SHOULD render those entries as read-only and sellers MUST echo them in package targeting_overlay.signal_targeting_groups. Use selection_group_rules for product-scoped products that need different behavior for different groups, such as fixed suppressions plus a required include tier.

min_selected_signals.description: Minimum number of signals the buyer must select when selection_mode is 'required'. If selection_mode is 'required' and this field is omitted, sellers MUST treat the minimum as 1. Defaults to 0 for optional selection.

max_selected_signals.description: Maximum number of signals the buyer may select for a package. Omit when there is no declared limit beyond the available options.

max_selected_per_group.description: Maximum number of signal_targeting_options the buyer may select from the same ProductSignalTargetingOption.selection_group. Use 1 for mutually exclusive alternatives within each option group. This limit applies to product option grouping, not to the number of child groups in packages[].targeting_overlay.signal_targeting_groups.

max_signal_targeting_groups.description: Maximum number of child groups allowed in packages[].targeting_overlay.signal_targeting_groups.groups. Omit when the seller has no declared limit beyond product terms.

max_signals_per_targeting_group.description: Maximum number of signals allowed in each packages[].targeting_overlay.signal_targeting_groups.groups[].signals array. Omit when the seller has no declared limit beyond product terms.

selection_group_rules.description: Optional product-scoped overrides for specific ProductSignalTargetingOption.selection_group values. Use this when one product has mixed behavior, such as fixed seller-applied suppressions, a required pick-one include tier, optional buyer-selected exclusions, or heterogeneous targeting planes that must be represented as separate ANDed clauses. Rules apply only to options whose selection_group matches. When selection_group_rules are present, each packages[].targeting_overlay.signal_targeting_groups child group MUST contain signals from exactly one selection_group and one targeting_mode, and buyers MUST send at most one child group for each (selection_group, targeting_mode) pair. Sellers MUST reject duplicate, mixed, or collapsed groups that combine distinct selection_group_rules into the same child group.

items.title: Signal Selection Group Rule
items.description: Product-scoped override for one ProductSignalTargetingOption.selection_group value. Use this when a product has mixed signal-selection behavior, such as fixed suppressions plus a required pick-one include tier.

targeting_mode.description: How options in this selection_group are intended to be used in signal_targeting_groups. 'include' maps to child groups with operator 'any'. 'exclude' maps to child groups with operator 'none'. Omit when options in the group may be used according to each option's allowed_targeting_modes.

selection_mode.description: Selection behavior for this selection_group. 'required' means at least min_selected_signals, or 1 when omitted. 'fixed' means default_selected options in this group are seller-applied and read-only.

min_selected_signals.description: Minimum selected options from this selection_group. If selection_mode is 'required' and omitted, sellers MUST treat the minimum as 1.

max_selected_signals.description: Maximum selected options from this selection_group.

signal_pricing_group_rules.description: Experimental (signals.pricing_groups). Product-scoped rules for how fees of signals sharing a pricing_group combine; they override get_signals signal_pricing_group_rules for the same pricing_group. A group with no rule is charged 'each', so a seller opts in to 'highest' explicitly. Ungrouped signals are always 'each'.

age.description: Age-targeting execution available for this product.

execution_modes.description: Ways this product can execute canonical age intent. continuous_bounds accepts canonical predicates whose explicit integer bounds fall between min_supported_age and max_supported_age, inclusive; omitted bounds additionally require the corresponding supports_unbounded_min or supports_unbounded_max flag. enumerated_intervals accepts exact unions of the declared intervals; signals resolves through signals carrying authoritative demographic_predicate metadata.

min_supported_age.description: Lowest integer accepted as an explicit min or max bound by continuous_bounds. This limit does not replace an omitted min: omission means no lower age restriction. Required when that execution mode is declared.

max_supported_age.description: Highest integer accepted as an explicit min or max bound by continuous_bounds. Required when that execution mode is declared.

supports_unbounded_min.description: Whether continuous_bounds accepts a predicate with min omitted. When true, the omitted min means no lower age restriction and MUST NOT be replaced by min_supported_age. When false, the seller MUST reject open-lower predicates. Required when continuous_bounds is declared.

supports_unbounded_max.description: Whether continuous_bounds accepts a predicate with max omitted. When true, the omitted max means no upper age restriction and MUST NOT be replaced by max_supported_age; for example, min 65 remains 65+. When false, the seller MUST reject open-upper predicates. Required when continuous_bounds is declared.

unknown_handling.description: How this product handles people whose age is unavailable. selectable honors either include_unknown value; always_excluded supports only false; always_included supports only true. supported_bases.description: User-level age determination bases this product can use for exact execution. Sellers MUST publish only bases whose provenance they can preserve and audit; they MUST NOT infer a basis from an opaque platform age bucket. enumDescriptions.declared: The user supplied an age, date of birth, or threshold affirmation without independent verification.
