hold_policy.title: Hold Policy
hold_policy.description: Experimental (media_buy.hold_policy). Planning hint: the inventory-hold policy the seller generally offers when finalizing a proposal that allocates this product, so buyers can plan before requesting one. It binds nothing; only a draft proposal's hold_policy binds, and the seller derives that from the allocated products when it creates the draft (a draft allocating a product whose effective policy is non-holdable declares available false). Not a reservation and no guarantee of availability. When absent, get_adcp_capabilities media_buy.proposal_refinement.hold_semantics applies (inventory_hold when that is also absent). Omitted for callers below 3.3.

available.description: Whether a successful finalize places an inventory hold. true means an exclusive, first-position hold: until expires_at, no other buyer's hold or booking takes the held inventory. Ranked holds are declared by the separate rankable field (#8086); available is not reinterpreted, so available true without rankable true keeps this exclusive, first-position meaning. false means finalize commits terms only for this entry (terms_only semantics): no hold, expires_at is the acceptance window, and the seller MUST NOT return hold_unavailable for the entry. A draft whose allocated products include any product whose effective policy is non-holdable MUST itself declare available false; there are no partial holds within a proposal. Declaring available false does not require listing media_buy.delegated_composition. As for hold_semantics terms_only, the seller MUST NOT return such a committed proposal to a caller whose adcp_version is below 3.3; it fails the request at task level with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.

min_duration.description: Minimum hold the seller promises. A successful finalize MUST set expires_at no earlier than the committed proposal's hold_placed_at plus this duration. A draft's min_duration MUST NOT exceed the max_duration of any allocated product that declares one.

max_duration.description: Longest initial hold the seller will place at finalize: expires_at MUST NOT be later than the committed proposal's hold_placed_at plus this duration. A draft's max_duration MUST NOT exceed the max_duration of any allocated product that declares one.

extendable.description: Whether the seller accepts refine_proposals action extend_hold (experimental, media_buy.hold_extension, gated by get_adcp_capabilities media_buy.proposal_refinement.hold_extension) for a hold placed under this policy. Defaults to false: when false or absent, the seller declines extend_hold with hold_unavailable and buyers SHOULD NOT send it. A draft is extendable only if every allocated product's effective policy is extendable. Each extension successor carries this policy forward unchanged.

max_total_duration.description: Ceiling on the total length of a hold placed under this policy, across the whole extension chain, measured from the original hold_placed_at (extended successors carry hold_placed_at forward). An extend_hold successor's expires_at MUST NOT exceed the original hold_placed_at plus this duration; an extension never resets it. Allowed only when extendable is true. A draft's max_total_duration MUST NOT exceed the max_total_duration of any allocated product that declares one.

rankable.description: Experimental (media_buy.hold_ranking). Whether a successful finalize may place this hold behind other buyers' holds on the same inventory. false or absent (the default) keeps the exclusive, first-position meaning of available true: the seller places a first-position hold or returns hold_unavailable. true means the hold is ranked: finalize may succeed with the hold queued behind holds that could prevent it from booking, and the committed proposal reports the buyer's own position in hold_rank (1 = first position). A hold at rank 1 has the same acceptance guarantee as an exclusive hold until expires_at. A hold behind first position (hold_rank 2 or more) does not: while a hold ahead of it is live or has been accepted, the seller MAY decline accept_proposal with PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE. Ranking is advisory: no right-of-first-refusal deadline and no rank-change notification are defined. A draft is rankable if any allocated product's effective policy is rankable. Allowed only when available is true. Each extend_hold successor carries this policy forward unchanged. For a caller below 3.3, which never receives hold_policy, the seller treats rankable as false.

allOf.description: Durations, extension, and ranking describe a hold, so they are forbidden when finalize places none.
A total ceiling only bounds extensions, so it requires extendable true.

collections.description: Experimental (media_buy.collection_cards). Full collection objects for collections referenced by the collections selectors of products on this page. Sellers MUST NOT return this array unless the request set include_collections to true; when it is set, sellers SHOULD include every referenced collection and MUST NOT include one that no returned product references. At most one entry per (publisher_domain, collection_id). If a key appears more than once, that collection is unresolvable from this response; buyers fall back to the publisher's adagents.json, as they do for an omitted collection, and ignore entries that no returned product references. These are convenience copies, never authorization evidence: a copy wins over adagents.json only on images, sample_content, url, description, season, cadence and distribution[].followers (see core/response-collection.json). Present only alongside products, so never on an unchanged outcome.

items.title: Response Collection

Full collection object returned in a product or proposal response for a collection that a returned product's collections selector references, by list_collections, or in a collection_card.updated webhook (experimental, media_buy.collection_catalog). For the same key, account and moment, a seller returns the same copy on every one of those surfaces. publisher_domain is required because collection_id is unique only within its publisher. Keyed by (publisher_domain, collection_id). This is a convenience copy from the selling agent: the publisher's adagents.json remains the root of authorization, and a response copy is never authorization evidence. The response copy wins over adagents.json only on images, sample_content, url, description, season, cadence and distribution[].followers; every other field, including status, talent, content_rating, genre, kind, special and the rest of distribution, stays anchored to adagents.json, as does which agent may sell the collection. An entry whose (publisher_domain, collection_id) is not declared in that publisher's adagents.json, or that comes from a selling agent adagents.json does not authorize for the collection, is unverified display data: it does not establish that the collection exists or is sellable, buyers MUST NOT present it as the publisher's declaration, and its distribution MUST NOT feed carriage verification.

allOf.title: Collection
allOf.description: A recurring inventory container — a named program, publication, event series, rotation, or programmed channel that produces bookable installments on a defined cadence. The kind field indicates how to interpret this collection: 'series' for TV/podcast programs, 'publication' for print/newsletter titles, 'event_series' for live events, 'rotation' for DOOH scheduling, and 'channel' for continuously programmed audio or video streams regardless of carriage or monetization model. Declared in the publisher's adagents.json and referenced by products via collection selectors. Selling agents may also return copies in product and proposal responses (core/response-collection.json); adagents.json remains the authorization source.

publisher_domain.description: Publisher namespace that owns this collection. Required for supply-path verification when the declaration is read from a cross-origin authoritative document; it must match the publisher whose origin delegated retrieval. A pointer alone cannot claim another publisher's collection. May be omitted for a publisher-origin document, where that origin supplies the namespace.

collection_id.description: Publisher-assigned identifier for this collection. Declared in the publisher's adagents.json collections array. Products reference collections via collection selectors with publisher_domain and collection_ids. Use distribution identifiers for cross-seller matching across publishers.

enumDescriptions.publication: Print or newsletter title; installments are issues

brand_ref.title: Brand Reference
brand_ref.description: Experimental (media_buy.collection_cards). Typed link to this person's brand in brand.json, for example a rights-holder brand with right_type talent. When brand_ref and brand_url are both present they MUST identify the same brand (brand_url's host equals brand_ref.domain), and brand_ref wins. Only domain and brand_id are read here; other brand_ref fields are ignored. The link is one-sided: buyers SHOULD treat it as confirmed only when that brand's get_brand_identity collections lists the same {publisher_domain, collection_id} back.

domain.description: Domain where /.well-known/brand.json is hosted, or the brand's operating domain

brand_id.title: Brand ID
brand_id.description: Brand within a brand.json that lists several brands. Optional for single-brand domains.

countries.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 countries the advertiser account serves. This is an account attribute: it does not identify the brand or the account, and it is not delivery targeting. Omit when the account is not limited to particular countries. Array order is not meaningful.

industries.description: Inline override for the brand's industries. Useful when the caller cannot modify the brand's canonical brand.json but needs to declare industries for governance (e.g., Annex III vertical detection). brand.json remains the canonical source; when omitted here, governance agents SHOULD resolve from brand.json.

data_subject_contestation.description: Inline override for the brand's contestation contact point. Useful when the operator does not control brand.json but needs to discharge Art 22(3) for this plan. brand.json is canonical; when omitted, governance agents resolve brand → house → missing.

brand_kit_override.description:
Inline override for brand-kit fields normally resolved from `/.well-known/brand.json` on `domain` (logo, colors, voice, tagline). Use when brand.json is missing, stale, or inappropriate for this specific call — e.g., a campaign-scoped tagline, a co-branded creative, a freshly-rebranded color palette the brand.json hasn't shipped yet. Same inline-override pattern as `industries` and `data_subject_contestation` above: brand.json is canonical, the override is per-call. Adopters needing to override fields outside this subset MUST publish a different brand.json and reference it via a different `domain` — the inline override is intentionally narrow to a small high-traffic subset. The brand-wide `prohibited_terms` list is one such field: it lives on brand.json and has no per-call override.

**Merge semantics (normative).** The merge is **field-level**, not whole-object replacement. Each field within `brand_kit_override` (`logo`, `colors`, `voice`, `tagline`) is evaluated independently — when a field is present on the override the override value applies; when a field is absent the brand.json value applies (or is absent if brand.json doesn't carry one either). For composite fields (`colors.primary`, `colors.secondary`, `colors.accent`), the merge is one level deeper: each color slot is evaluated independently — a producer can override `colors.primary` while still inheriting `colors.secondary` from brand.json. SDKs MUST NOT treat a present `brand_kit_override.colors` as wiping the brand.json `colors` block entirely; only the per-slot fields present in the override take precedence. Without this rule, a partial-override semantics would diverge across SDKs and produce inconsistent rendering for the same payload.

items.description: Reference to an already-published post on a publisher, creator, or social platform. The buyer supplies a reference to the existing post; the seller resolves, authorizes, reviews, and serves the referenced post according to the target product's format declaration. This asset is for post references, not uploaded bytes and not catalog rows.

distribution.description: Where this collection is distributed. Each entry maps the collection to a publisher platform using host property IDs, identifiers, or both. For channel collections this is the carriage map. It is a publisher assertion for discovery, not sales authorization; buyers validate owner-sold carriage against the host publisher's collection-scoped authorized_agents declaration. Collections SHOULD include at least one platform-independent identifier (imdb_id, gracenote_id, eidr_id) when available.

items.title: Collection Distribution
items.description: A collection's presence on a specific publisher platform. For a channel collection, this is a carriage assertion: property_ids identify the host surfaces carrying the channel, while identifiers identify the channel in the host's catalog or an independent metadata system. This publisher-authored assertion supports discovery and cross-seller matching but does not authorize a sale; authorization remains rooted in the host publisher's collection-scoped authorized_agents entry.

publisher_domain.description: Domain of the publisher platform where the collection is distributed (e.g., 'youtube.com', 'spotify.com'). Property IDs and publisher-scoped identifiers in this object resolve in this publisher's namespace.

property_ids.description: Publisher-scoped property IDs from publisher_domain's adagents.json that carry this collection. For owner-sold channel inventory, these identify the host apps without requiring the host to publish channel-owner placement definitions.

items.title: Property ID
items.description: Identifier for a publisher property. Must be lowercase alphanumeric with underscores only.

identifiers.description: Identifiers for the collection on this publisher, including publisher-scoped channel/EPG identifiers and platform-independent metadata identifiers

enumDescriptions.youtube_channel_id: YouTube channel ID. Preferred canonical identifier for YouTube channels; handles and URLs are discovery aliases that should resolve to this when possible.
enumDescriptions.youtube_channel_handle: YouTube channel handle such as @example. Useful as a discovery alias; channel ID is preferred for canonical matching.
enumDescriptions.youtube_channel_url: YouTube channel URL such as https://www.youtube.com/@example or https://www.youtube.com/channel/UC.... Useful as a discovery alias; channel ID is preferred for canonical matching.
enumDescriptions.youtube_playlist_id: YouTube playlist ID (for series within a channel)
enumDescriptions.platform_channel_id: Stable channel identifier assigned by the platform named in the enclosing distribution's publisher_domain. Use as the portable fallback when no platform-specific identifier type exists; identity is the tuple (publisher_domain, value), so this type is only meaningful inside a distribution entry and MUST NOT appear in bare {type, value} contexts (distribution_ids sources, exclude filters). Use the platform's stable catalog identifier, not an EPG position number — hosts renumber lineups.
enumDescriptions.gracenote_id: Gracenote TMS ID — industry standard for TV metadata
enumDescriptions.eidr_id: EIDR (Entertainment Identifier Registry) — ISO 10528 for audiovisual content

followers.title: Audience Size
followers.description: Experimental in AdCP 3.3. Platform-reported number of follower or subscriber accounts for this collection on publisher_domain (the audience-size wording about people does not apply). Counts accounts, not de-duplicated people, so buyers MUST NOT sum it across distribution entries or read it as reach. Use precision 'approximate' when the platform rounds publicly (for example, public subscriber counts); as_of is when the count last changed, not when it was last read: a refresh that leaves lower_bound, upper_bound and precision unchanged is not a change: it keeps the earlier as_of, moves no version token, and fires no webhook. Display and comparison only: this is not a targeting predicate and does not size a buyable audience. A seller serving or relaying it MUST list media_buy.collection_cards in experimental_features on get_adcp_capabilities.

lower_bound.description: Lowest number of people the size can be. Equals upper_bound when precision is 'exact'.

upper_bound.description: Highest number of people the size can be. MUST be greater than or equal to lower_bound.

precision.title: Audience Size Precision
precision.description: How precisely lower_bound and upper_bound are reported.

enumDescriptions.exact: The seller reports a single exact value. lower_bound MUST equal upper_bound.
enumDescriptions.approximate: The seller reports an approximation, or an interval it computed or was given for privacy or freshness reasons. The true size is expected to fall within lower_bound and upper_bound, but the seller does not commit to exact values.
enumDescriptions.bucketed: The seller reports a coarse size bucket. lower_bound and upper_bound are the bucket edges and carry no information beyond the bucket the audience falls in.

as_of.description: ISO 8601 timestamp of when the seller or its platform computed this size. Omitted when the seller does not know. Sizes drift as membership and matching change, so buyers comparing two reads should compare as_of first.

deadline_policy.title: Deadline Policy
deadline_policy.description: Default deadline rules for installments of this collection. Agents compute absolute deadlines from each installment's scheduled_at and these lead times. Installments with explicit deadlines override this policy. Only meaningful when installments carry scheduled_at; a continuously programmed channel collection without enumerated installments has no deadlines to derive.

booking_lead_days.description: Days before scheduled_at by which the placement must be booked

cancellation_lead_days.description: Days before scheduled_at by which cancellation is penalty-free

material_stages.description: Default material submission stages. Items MUST be in chronological order (earliest due first). Agents compute due_at as: installment.scheduled_at minus lead_days.

stage.description: Stage identifier. Standard values: 'draft' (needs seller processing), 'final' (production-ready).

lead_days.description: Days before scheduled_at this stage is due

label.description: What the seller needs at this stage

business_days_only.description: When true, lead_days counts business days (Mon-Fri) rather than calendar days. Defaults to false.

related_collections.description: Relationships to other collections (spin-offs, companion collections, etc.). Each entry references another collection by collection_id within the same publisher's adagents.json.

collection_id.description: The related collection's collection_id within this seller's response

enumDescriptions.spinoff: A collection derived from the referenced collection (e.g., an after-collection or character spinoff)
enumDescriptions.companion: A companion collection (behind-the-scenes, reaction, or supplementary content)
enumDescriptions.sequel: A continuation of the referenced collection
enumDescriptions.prequel: A predecessor to the referenced collection
enumDescriptions.crossover: Shows that share installments, guests, or story arcs

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page. Omitted when this is the last page.

feed_version.description: Opaque version of the selected offer feed. Scoped to the selection, including include_collections: without it collection copies are outside the version, and with it the version also changes when any returned collection copy changes; sellers issue distinct tokens for the two settings. For wholesale webhook consumers this is the same scope-keyed token carried as wholesale_feed_version on product.* and wholesale_feed.bulk_change notifications.

pricing_version.description: Opaque version of the selected pricing layer.

incomplete.description: Usable partial response with explicitly missing product-list scopes.

estimated_wait.title: Duration
estimated_wait.description: A time duration expressed as an interval and unit. Used for frequency cap windows, attribution windows, reach optimization windows, time budgets, and other time-based settings. When unit is 'campaign', interval must be 1 — the window spans the full campaign flight.

interval.description: Number of time units. Must be 1 when unit is 'campaign'.

unit.description: Time unit. 'seconds' for sub-minute precision. 'campaign' spans the full campaign flight.

context.title: Context Object
context.description: Opaque correlation data that is echoed unchanged in responses. Used for internal tracking, UI session IDs, trace IDs, and other caller-specific identifiers that don't affect protocol behavior. Context data is never parsed by AdCP agents - it's simply preserved and returned.

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

Provenance.title: Provenance
Provenance.description: Declares how content was produced, whether AI was involved, and what disclosure obligations apply. Attaches to creative manifests, individual assets, or content-standards artifacts. When present at multiple levels, the most specific provenance object replaces the inherited one entirely (no field-level merging). Provenance is a claim by the declaring party — receiving parties should verify claims independently via their own detection tools.

digital_source_type.title: Digital Source Type
digital_source_type.description: IPTC-aligned classification of AI involvement in producing this content

enumDescriptions.digital_capture: Captured by a digital device (camera, scanner, screen recording) with no AI involvement
enumDescriptions.digital_creation: Created by a human using digital tools (Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects) without AI generation
enumDescriptions.trained_algorithmic_media: Generated entirely by a trained AI model (DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Sora)
enumDescriptions.composite_with_trained_algorithmic_media: Human-created content combined with AI-generated elements (e.g., photo with AI background)
enumDescriptions.algorithmic_media: Produced by deterministic algorithms without machine learning (procedural generation, rule-based systems)
enumDescriptions.composite_capture: Multiple digital captures composited together without AI
enumDescriptions.composite_synthetic: Composite of multiple elements where at least one is AI-generated (e.g., stock photo composited with AI-generated background)
enumDescriptions.human_edits: Content augmented, corrected, or enhanced by humans using non-generative tools
enumDescriptions.data_driven_media: Assembled from structured data feeds (DCO templates, product catalogs, weather-triggered variants)

synthetic_depiction.description: Assessed declaration of whether the content synthetically depicts a real or fictional person performing or appearing in a way that was generated or materially manipulated rather than captured as depicted. `true` covers both a fully synthetic performer and material manipulation of a real performer; `false` is an assessed declaration that the content does not contain such a depiction. Absence means the content has not been assessed for synthetic depiction. This field does not claim consent, legality, or independent verification, and receivers MUST NOT derive it solely from `digital_source_type`.

ai_tool.description: AI system used to generate or modify this content. Aligns with IPTC 2025.1 AI metadata fields and C2PA claim_generator.

name.description: Name of the AI tool or model (e.g., 'DALL-E 3', 'Stable Diffusion XL', 'Gemini')

version.description: Version identifier for the AI tool or model (e.g., '25.1', '0125', '2.1'). For generative models, use the model version rather than the API version.

provider.description: Organization that provides the AI tool (e.g., 'OpenAI', 'Stability AI', 'Google')

human_oversight.description: Level of human involvement in the AI-assisted creation process. Independent of `disclosure.required` — the protocol does not derive disclosure obligations from oversight level. Some regulations include carve-outs for human-edited or human-directed AI output, but those carve-outs have factual prerequisites the schema cannot evaluate. Asserting `edited` or `directed` does not by itself justify `disclosure.required: false`.

enumDescriptions.none: Fully automated with no human involvement in generation
enumDescriptions.prompt_only: Human provided the prompt or instructions but did not review outputs
enumDescriptions.selected: Human selected from multiple AI-generated candidates
enumDescriptions.edited: Human edited or refined AI-generated output
enumDescriptions.directed: Human directed the creative process with AI as an assistive tool

declared_by.description: Party declaring this provenance. Identifies who attached the provenance claim, enabling receiving parties to assess trust.

agent_url.description: URL of the agent or service that declared this provenance

role.description: Role of the declaring party in the supply chain

enumDescriptions.creator: The party that created or generated the content
enumDescriptions.advertiser: The brand or advertiser that owns the content
enumDescriptions.agency: Agency acting on behalf of the advertiser
enumDescriptions.platform: Ad platform or publisher that processed the content
enumDescriptions.tool: Automated tool or service that attached provenance metadata

declared_at.description: When this provenance claim was made (ISO 8601). Distinct from created_time, which records when the content itself was produced. A provenance claim may be attached well after content creation, for example when retroactively declaring AI involvement for regulatory compliance.

created_time.description: When this content was created or generated (ISO 8601)

c2pa.description: C2PA sidecar manifest reference. Links to a detached cryptographic provenance manifest for this content. Note: file-level C2PA bindings break when ad servers transcode, resize, or re-encode assets. For pipelines with intermediaries, consider embedded_provenance as the primary provenance mechanism.

manifest_url.description: URL to the C2PA manifest store for this content

embedded_provenance.description: Provenance metadata embedded within the content stream. Each entry declares one embedding layer: structured provenance data carried inside the content itself, as distinct from sidecar references (c2pa.manifest_url). Embedded provenance survives operations that break sidecar and file-level bindings: ad-server transcoding, CMS ingestion, copy-paste, reformatting, and CDN re-encoding. For ad-tech pipelines where content passes through multiple intermediaries, embedded provenance is the reliable path for provenance that persists from declaration through delivery. This is a declaration by the embedding party. The receiving party (the seller) is the verifier-of-record: it confirms the claim by calling a governance agent it trusts (typically one published in `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers`).

method.title: Embedded Provenance Method
method.description: How provenance data is carried within the content

enumDescriptions.manifest_wrapper: A provenance manifest embedded in the file container per format-specific rules (e.g., JUMBF box in JPEG, C2PATextManifestWrapper in plaintext per C2PA Section A.7). The manifest travels with the file but is tied to the file's byte structure.
enumDescriptions.provenance_markers: Invisible markers embedded within the content stream that encode or reference a provenance record. Designed to survive reformatting, copy-paste, CMS ingestion, and ad-server transcoding that breaks file-level bindings.

standard.description: Standard the embedding conforms to, if any (e.g., 'c2pa' for C2PA Section A.7 text manifest embedding)

provider.description: Organization that performed the embedding (e.g., 'Encypher', 'Digimarc'). Display label and audit context — not a wire identifier.

verify_agent.description: Buyer's representation that this embedding can be verified by a governance agent on the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers` list. The `agent_url` MUST match (canonicalized) one of the seller's published `accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` entries; sellers reject `sync_creatives` submissions whose `verify_agent.agent_url` is off-list with `PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_NOT_ACCEPTED`. This is buyer-supplied evidence, not buyer-driven routing — the seller is the verifier-of-record and the seller controls which agent it actually calls (the seller MAY use a different on-list agent if it determines this is more appropriate; the seller does not call buyer-asserted endpoints outside its allowlist). MAY be omitted for self-verifiable embeddings (e.g., a C2PA text manifest with a public key the seller already trusts).

agent_url.description: URL of the governance agent the buyer represents was used to embed/verify this layer. MUST use the `https://` scheme and MUST appear in the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` list (canonicalized per /docs/reference/url-canonicalization: lowercase scheme and host, strip default port, normalize path dot-segments). Sellers MUST NOT call this URL until the canonicalized match is confirmed.

feature_id.description: Optional `feature_id` the buyer represents the seller should request via `get_creative_features` (e.g., `encypher.markers_present_v2`). SHOULD match the `feature_id` declared on the matching `accepted_verifiers[]` entry, or be omitted to defer the selector to the seller. When the seller's entry pins a `feature_id`, that value wins; when neither side pins, the seller selects from the agent's `governance.creative_features` catalog.

embedded_at.description: When the provenance data was embedded (ISO 8601)

watermarks.description: Content watermarks applied to this asset. Each entry declares one watermarking layer: a content modification that encodes an identifier or fingerprint within the asset. Watermarks differ from embedded provenance: a watermark encodes an identifier (who generated it, who owns it), while embedded provenance carries or references a structured provenance record (the full chain of custody). A single asset may carry both. Aligns with C2PA action taxonomy: c2pa.watermarked.bound (watermark linked to a C2PA manifest) and c2pa.watermarked.unbound (watermark independent of any manifest). This is a declaration by the watermarking party. The receiving party (the seller) is the verifier-of-record: it confirms the claim by calling a governance agent it trusts (typically one published in `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers`).

media_type.title: Watermark Media Type
media_type.description: Media category of the watermarked content

enumDescriptions.audio: Watermark applied to audio content (e.g., spread-spectrum, echo hiding)
enumDescriptions.image: Watermark applied to image content (e.g., spatial domain, frequency domain)
enumDescriptions.video: Watermark applied to video content (e.g., per-frame image watermarking, temporal watermarking)
enumDescriptions.text: Watermark applied to text content (e.g., synonym substitution, structural modification)

provider.description: Organization that applied the watermark (e.g., 'Imatag', 'Steg.AI', 'Encypher'). Display label and audit context — not a wire identifier.

verify_agent.description: Buyer's representation that this watermark can be detected by a governance agent on the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers` list. The `agent_url` MUST match (canonicalized) one of the seller's published `accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` entries; sellers reject `sync_creatives` submissions whose `verify_agent.agent_url` is off-list with `PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_NOT_ACCEPTED`. This is buyer-supplied evidence, not buyer-driven routing — the seller is the verifier-of-record and the seller controls which agent it actually calls (the seller MAY use a different on-list agent if it determines this is more appropriate; the seller does not call buyer-asserted endpoints outside its allowlist).

agent_url.description: URL of the governance agent the buyer represents was used to apply/detect this watermark. MUST use the `https://` scheme and MUST appear in the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` list (canonicalized per /docs/reference/url-canonicalization: lowercase scheme and host, strip default port, normalize path dot-segments). Sellers MUST NOT call this URL until the canonicalized match is confirmed.

feature_id.description: Optional `feature_id` the buyer represents the seller should request via `get_creative_features` (e.g., `imatag.watermark_detected`). SHOULD match the `feature_id` declared on the matching `accepted_verifiers[]` entry, or be omitted to defer the selector to the seller. When the seller's entry pins a `feature_id`, that value wins; when neither side pins, the seller selects from the agent's `governance.creative_features` catalog.

c2pa_action.title: C2PA Watermark Action
c2pa_action.description: C2PA action classification for this watermark

enumDescriptions.c2pa.watermarked.bound: Watermark linked to a C2PA manifest for this asset. The watermark and manifest are mutually reinforcing: the manifest references the watermark, and the watermark can be used to locate the manifest.
enumDescriptions.c2pa.watermarked.unbound: Watermark independent of any C2PA manifest. Applied before any provenance signing event (e.g., by the AI generator at creation time) or in pipelines where no manifest is present.

disclosure.description: Regulatory disclosure requirements for this content. Indicates whether AI disclosure is required and under which jurisdictions.

required.description: The declaring party's claim that AI disclosure is required for this content under applicable regulations. This is a declared signal carried through the supply chain — useful as a routing and audit input — not a regulatory determination made by the protocol. Receiving parties remain responsible for their own jurisdictional analysis and should not treat `required: false` as compliance cover.

region.description: Sub-national region code (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'BY' for Bavaria)

label_text.description: Required disclosure label text for this jurisdiction, in the local language

render_guidance.description: How the disclosure should be rendered for this jurisdiction. Expresses the declaring party's intent for persistence and position based on regulatory requirements. Publishers control actual rendering but governance agents can audit whether guidance was followed.

persistence.title: Disclosure Persistence
persistence.description: How long the disclosure must persist during content playback or display

enumDescriptions.continuous: Disclosure must remain visible or audible throughout the entire content display duration. For video and audio, this means the full playback duration. For static formats (display, DOOH), this means the full display slot. For DOOH specifically, 'content duration' means the ad's display slot within the rotation, not the screen's full rotation cycle.
enumDescriptions.initial: Disclosure must appear at the start of content for a minimum duration before it may be removed. Pair with min_duration_ms in render_guidance or creative brief to specify the required duration.
enumDescriptions.flexible: Disclosure presence is sufficient; placement timing and duration are at the publisher's discretion

min_duration_ms.description: Minimum display duration in milliseconds for initial persistence. Recommended when persistence is initial — without it, the duration is at the publisher's discretion. At serve time the publisher reads this from provenance since the brief is not available.

positions.description: Preferred disclosure positions in priority order. The first position a format supports should be used.

items.title: Disclosure Position
items.description: Where a required disclosure should appear within a creative. Used by creative briefs to specify disclosure placement and by formats to declare which positions they can render.

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

verification.description: Third-party verification or detection results for this content. Multiple services may independently evaluate the same content. Provenance is a claim — verification results attached by the declaring party are supplementary. The enforcing party (e.g., seller/publisher) should run its own verification via get_creative_features or calibrate_content.

verified_by.description: Name of the verification service (e.g., 'DoubleVerify', 'Hive Moderation', 'Reality Defender')

confidence.description: Confidence score of the verification result (0.0 to 1.0)

details_url.description: URL to the full verification report

ext.title: Extension Object
ext.description: Extension object for optional parameters under an owner-controlled namespace (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). The reserved ext.adcp namespace is maintained by the AdCP Working Group and is limited to its documented bindings. Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization. Namespace support does not imply support for undocumented future bindings.

MediaChannel.title: Media Channel
MediaChannel.description: Standardized advertising media channels describing how buyers allocate budget. Channels are planning abstractions, not technical substrates. See the Media Channel Taxonomy specification for detailed definitions.

enumDescriptions.display: Digital display advertising (banners, native, rich media) across web and app
enumDescriptions.olv: Online video advertising outside CTV (pre-roll, outstream, in-app video)
enumDescriptions.social: Social media platforms (Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn, etc.)
enumDescriptions.search: Search engine advertising and search networks
enumDescriptions.ctv: Connected TV and streaming on television screens
enumDescriptions.streaming_audio: Digital audio streaming services (Spotify, Pandora, etc.)
enumDescriptions.dooh: Digital out-of-home buying context, including inventory on venue-operated screens and audio players
enumDescriptions.print: Newspapers, magazines, and other print publications
enumDescriptions.email: Email advertising and sponsored newsletter content
enumDescriptions.retail_media: Retail media networks and commerce marketplaces (Amazon, Walmart, Instacart)
enumDescriptions.affiliate: Affiliate networks, comparison sites, and performance-based partnerships
enumDescriptions.product_placement: Product placement, branded content, and sponsorship integrations
enumDescriptions.sponsored_intelligence: Sponsored Intelligence — advertising within AI assistants, AI search, and generative AI experiences via the reversed data flow

VideoPlacementType.title: Video Placement Type
VideoPlacementType.description: Declared video placement classification for OLV and other video inventory, using the IAB Tech Lab/OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt definitions with AdCP-native value names. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.instream: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=1: video ads played before, during, or after streaming video content requested by the user.
enumDescriptions.accompanying_content: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=2: video ads played with accompanying video content in a player associated with the page or app content.
enumDescriptions.interstitial: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=3: video ads shown as an interstitial experience, typically between content or app states.
enumDescriptions.standalone: OpenRTB 2.6 video.plcmt=4: video ads shown without associated video content, also called no-content or standalone video.

AudioDistributionType.title: Audio Distribution Type
AudioDistributionType.description: Declared audio distribution classification for radio, streaming-audio, podcast, and other audio inventory, using IAB Tech Lab/OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed definitions with AdCP-native value names. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.fm_am_broadcast: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=2: FM/AM broadcast, including live content broadcast over the air and also available via online streaming.
enumDescriptions.podcast: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=3: original, pre-recorded content distributed as episodes in a series.
enumDescriptions.catch_up_radio: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=4: recorded segment of a radio show that was originally broadcast live.
enumDescriptions.web_radio: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=5: live audio content only available via online streaming, not as FM/AM broadcast.
enumDescriptions.video_game: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=6: background audio in video games.
enumDescriptions.text_to_speech: OpenRTB 2.6 audio.feed=7: text-to-speech audio such as audio books or website/plugin article narration.

SponsoredPlacementType.title: Sponsored Placement Type
SponsoredPlacementType.description: Declared sponsored-placement classification for catalog-driven retail-media inventory, distinguishing where the sponsored placement renders on the retailer surface. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.sponsored_search: Sponsored placements rendered against retailer on-site search results, keyed to the shopper's query (e.g., Amazon Sponsored Products on search, Walmart Connect Sponsored Search).
enumDescriptions.sponsored_display: Sponsored placements rendered in display slots across retailer browse, category, and product-detail pages outside the search results stream (e.g., Criteo Sponsored Display, Amazon Sponsored Display on-site).
enumDescriptions.sponsored_native: Sponsored placements rendered using the retailer's native in-grid product template, blending into the organic product listing (e.g., CitrusAd native product cards, Pinterest catalog-driven collections).

SocialPlacementSurface.title: Social Placement Surface
SocialPlacementSurface.description: Declared social-placement surface classification for social inventory, distinguishing the in-app surface where a social placement renders. Values name the semantic surface, not platform brands. This is seller-declared discovery metadata, not independent verification of inventory quality or delivery context.

enumDescriptions.feed: The primary scrolling home or timeline surface where posts and ads are interleaved with followed and recommended content.
enumDescriptions.stories: The full-screen, ephemeral tap-through surface presented between or alongside users' story content.
enumDescriptions.short_video: The full-screen, sound-on, swipe-past, algorithmically-recommended vertical short-video surface. Subsumes the platform brand names for this surface (Reels, Shorts, Spotlight, and TikTok's For You short-video experience) — platform identity belongs to a property/publisher axis, not here.
enumDescriptions.explore: The discovery or browse surface presenting recommended content outside the user's followed graph.
enumDescriptions.search: The in-app search-results surface, keyed to the user's query.

PixelTrackingEvent.title: Pixel Tracking Event
PixelTrackingEvent.description: Closed AdCP event vocabulary for renderer-fired pixel trackers. Impression and viewability values through `viewable_video_50` map to IAB OpenRTB Native event tracker types 1-4. `audible_video_complete` is an AdCP-defined first-class event, not an assigned IAB Native event type; Native reserves 500+ for exchange-specific use. `start`, `first_quartile`, `midpoint`, `third_quartile` and `complete` (added in 3.3.0) are AdCP-defined playback events with the same meaning as the VAST events of the same name, spelled in snake_case to match this enum; they apply to formats with a playback timeline (`video_hosted`, `audio_hosted`) and are ignored on formats without one, like `viewable_video_50`. `click` represents Native click trackers and `custom` is the explicit adopter-defined extension point.

enumDescriptions.impression: Fires when the ad is served (IAB Native event type 1).
enumDescriptions.viewable_mrc_50: IAB MRC viewable: 50% of pixels in view for at least 1 second (IAB Native event type 2).
enumDescriptions.viewable_mrc_100: IAB MRC viewable: 100% of pixels in view for at least 1 second (IAB Native event type 3).
enumDescriptions.viewable_video_50: Video viewable: 50% of pixels in view for at least 2 seconds; audio not required (IAB Native event type 4). Ignored on formats with no playback timeline.
enumDescriptions.audible_video_complete: AdCP-defined: the creative played to 100% completion with audio on. The audio-on variant of `complete`.
enumDescriptions.start: Playback of the creative begins. Same meaning as VAST `start`. Added in 3.3.0.
enumDescriptions.first_quartile: 25% of the creative's duration has played. Same meaning as VAST `firstQuartile`. Added in 3.3.0.
enumDescriptions.midpoint: 50% of the creative's duration has played. Same meaning as VAST `midpoint`. Added in 3.3.0.
enumDescriptions.third_quartile: 75% of the creative's duration has played. Same meaning as VAST `thirdQuartile`. Added in 3.3.0.
enumDescriptions.complete: The creative played to the end, whether or not audio was on. Same meaning as VAST `complete`; `audible_video_complete` is the audio-on variant. Added in 3.3.0.
enumDescriptions.click: Fires when the user clicks the creative (IAB Native click trackers).

TrackerExecutionActor.title: Tracker Execution Actor
TrackerExecutionActor.description: Actor responsible for initiating a buyer-supplied tracker under a seller-authored execution contract. This v1 vocabulary is intentionally narrower than the macro resolver actor vocabulary.

PriceAdjustmentKind.title: Price Adjustment Kind
PriceAdjustmentKind.description: Categorizes how a price adjustment affects the transaction

enumDescriptions.fee: Increases the price the buyer pays and the revenue the seller receives. Applied between list_price and the seller's fixed_price (e.g., ad serving fees, data/targeting surcharges, brand safety verification).
enumDescriptions.discount: Reduces the price the buyer pays and the revenue the seller receives. Applied between list_price and the seller's fixed_price (e.g., volume discounts, negotiated rates, early booking).
enumDescriptions.commission: Does not change the buyer's price or budget. Represents a revenue split — the portion retained by an intermediary (e.g., agency commission). Budgets are managed inclusive of commissions.
enumDescriptions.settlement: Does not change the committed price or budget. Applied at invoicing or payment time (e.g., cash discount for early payment). Informational for buyer agents; affects actual settlement amount.
enumDescriptions.operator_fee: Increases the price the advertiser pays without changing the seller's revenue: a fee the account's operator (e.g., an agency buying for a brand) or its buying platform keeps out of the advertiser's budget. Like fee, rate is a markup on the running price. Applied after every fee and discount; the running price before the first operator_fee is the seller's price. Only the operator's buying platform adds it, in breakdowns returned to the operator and the advertiser; sellers MUST NOT author it.

ReportingFrequency.title: Reporting Frequency
ReportingFrequency.description: Available frequencies for delivery reports and metrics updates. Weekly and quarterly match audience-currency publication cycles in measured channels (e.g. weekly OOH/radio increments, quarterly circulation updates); post_campaign is a single report after the flight ends. Buy-side agents MUST treat a product's declared frequencies as an optimization-eligibility gate: a buyer MUST NOT make mid-flight optimization decisions against metrics whose declared cadence is quarterly or post_campaign — such data describes a period that has closed, and optimizing on it means acting on a model of the channel that is false at decision time.

AvailableMetric.title: Available Metric
AvailableMetric.description: Standard delivery and performance metrics available for reporting. Most values name flat numeric fields of `core/delivery-metrics.json`. Leaf identities address a single numeric value nested inside an object-shaped metric so it can be declared, committed, aggregated, and sorted individually: `quartile_25`/`quartile_50`/`quartile_75`/`quartile_100` resolve to `quartile_data.q1_views`–`q4_views`, and `viewable_rate`/`viewable_impressions`/`measurable_impressions`/`viewed_seconds` resolve to the same-named fields of `viewability`. Structured nested identities `viewed_seconds_percentiles` and `viewed_seconds_histogram` make the corresponding optional distribution carriers discoverable, committable, and requestable, but not aggregatable or sortable. The nested object or array remains the canonical carrier — nested identities never introduce duplicate flat response fields. Container tokens such as `viewability`, `quartile_data`, `dooh_metrics`, and `time_based_views` declare their documented nested surface. **Container subsumption applies only to numeric leaves**: `viewability` subsumes `viewable_rate`, `viewable_impressions`, `measurable_impressions`, and `viewed_seconds`; `quartile_data` subsumes `quartile_25`, `quartile_50`, `quartile_75`, and `quartile_100`. This rule applies to capability declaration, `required_metrics` filtering, format `reported_metrics` intersection, and `requested_metrics` selection. Optional structured identities MUST be declared explicitly: `viewability` alone does not satisfy `viewed_seconds_percentiles` or `viewed_seconds_histogram`. Requesting any nested identity selects its canonical carrier in the response. A nested identity declaration does not imply sibling values or the carrier's non-metric fields.

Product mutability describes implementation capability; MediaBuy.available_actions remains authoritative for a live buy.

Visual placements may declare screen_resolution and motion; audio-only placements omit those screen-specific fields. For publisher_ref placements, product slot and loop values override publisher defaults while repeated screen_resolution and motion values must equal the publisher facts.
